positions.title: Software Development Engineer
positions.description:
Full Stack Software Engineer for the Azure Internet of Things SaaS offering, IoT Central.

- Architected the addition of custom role-based access control to IoT Central, Microsoft’s IoT SaaS offering, end to end
- Designed and published internal npm libraries to secure backend microservices under the new access control model
- Supported microservice owners in onboarding their endpoints to the correct permission scope
- Implemented backend microservice logic for creating and managing custom roles, assigning these custom roles to users, and verifying the user has the requested access
- Implemented the User Experience for creating custom roles, including managing permission dependencies between resources, editing existing roles, and bulk role management
- Shipped this feature in public preview as part of the Microsoft Ignite 2019 developer conference
- Prototyped a mobile application for the mass provisioning of Raspberry Pis as IoT devices into an IoT Central Application as part of the Azure IoT Hackathon and placed 2nd
- Further developed and delivered this project to meet the needs of our customers and field sales team, working extensively in React Native and device-side Nodejs to provision the phone itself as an IoT device, drawing upon onboard sensors such as the accelerometer and gyroscope
- Developed and released the Azure IoT Central Powershell extension

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
Interned on the Intune Fabric Health and Recovery team for two consecutive summers.

- Designed an HTTP client/provider stack from the ground up that allows engineers to make diagnostic calls to the Microsoft Service Fabric through a dynamic web portal
- Implemented the above design within the existing Intune diagnostic framework for immediate deployment, taking my design from concept to reality
- Developed an automated storage backup and recovery tool to allow incremental data recovery in the event of data corruption or datacenter disaster using the Azure Webjobs framework
- Prototyped, developed, and deployed business logic and UI updates to diagnose faulty partition replicas through the Intune Diagnostic Terminal
- Prototyped an Intune service call visualizer using the Neo4j persistent graph database Java API for preemptive diagnosis of overburdened nodes in the Enterprise Content Management (ECM) Hackathon and placed 1st

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
- Designed and developed a persistent graph database using the Neo4j Java API as a preferred alternative to RISC’s Perl-based cloud migration software
- Briefly experimented with alternatives for interactive viewing of generated BIRT reports, implementing iHub and other leading providers in the AWS EC2 environment

positions.title: Camp Counselor and Sailing Instructor
positions.description: Instructed students on the proper technique for sailing a formal sailing regatta and tested their ability to competently perform these operations.
